newsitem.title: UK: Euro-bourses and Wall St cast off rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Euro-bourses and Wall St cast off rate fears.

text.p: European stock markets staged a dramatic turnaround on Friday as U.S. economic data eased worries about an early rise in interest rates and Wall Street repaired part of Thursday's damage.
After starting the day with sharp falls following Wall Street's 160 point slump, confidence slowly returned to Europe's main bourses and London, Paris and Frankfurt all ended with gains.
As European markets closed for the weekend, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up nearly one percent or 70 points.

The dollar, which bounced higher after U.S. retail sales figures on Thursday strengthened the argument for a rate rise, came under late selling pressure in Europe after benign producer prices offset some rate rise expectations.
"The subdued producer price data erased some of the interest rate rise speculation generated by the retail sales figures," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
By the time Europe closed the dollar had slid to 1.6935 marks, well down from its high of 1.7100. Against the yen it slipped to 123.25, nearly one yen down on its peak of 124.11.

"The dollar will now keep an eye on next week's consumer price data," Stamenkovic added. "In terms of rate rise hopes, we have retail sales growing above trend but if inflation remains on the soft side, support for the dollar might be waning."

The PPI's biggest fall since October 1994 leaves the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve, in a difficult position as it prepares for its policy-setting meeting on March 25, New York economists and traders said.

"It gets back to the core question as to whether or not they (the Fed) should be pre-emptive and they are probably doing some soul-searching right now," said Tom Benfer, a director of foreign exchange at Bank of Montreal in New York. "If they tighten the rate structure, politically they will get a lot of flak."
After an initial sharp markdown in European stock values, investors kept their nerve and the main markets had already recouped most of their losses before Wall Street opened.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, ended with the FTSE 100 index gaining 26 points, or 0.6 percent, to 4,424.3.
Dealers said the market's ability to close above the key 4,400 mark boded well. "There are still a lot of shorts out there. I think we'll see the market squeeze higher," said one senior dealer.

Credit Lyonnais Laing equity strategist Cory Miller added: "Valuations in the UK are looking a little bit stretched. But the fact is that the market still has a strong undertone. Institutions are still looking to get back into the market."

Among individual shares, B.A.T Industries Plc , the most actively traded in London, fell 13p to 541-1/2p in the wake of a Mississippi court ruling that sent U.S. tobacco stocks sharply lower on Thursday.

Paris, which suffered the biggest decline of the major bourses in early trade, ended with the CAC-40 index posting a rise of 13 points to 2,645.62. "People felt reassured by the U.S. figures," one trader said.
However, he called the rebound partly technical after its recent falls. Brokers said support levels around 2,600 points had held well under the earlier selling pressure.
Renault resumed its advance, rising 5.4 percent to 139.40 francs.
"Investors are feeling more confident that they'll push through their restructuring plans," a trader said.
The German market, the worst performer of the big three on Thursday, got a strong boost from the U.S. data and ended bourse floor trade with a gain of 9.48 points at 3,359.29.
Share prices rose strongly in later screen-based trade with the IBIS DAX index putting on 36 points, or 1.08 percent, to 3,404.29.
"We are clearly in a period of extreme volatility. We are going to have to get used to it," said a Frankfurt dealer.
Chemical shares rebounded from lows hit this week after disappointing news from Hoechst AG that it had abandoned plans to list its HMR drugs unit.
Daimler-Benz AG got a major boost after a well-received analysts' meeting and news of plans to set up a traffic navigation joint venture with Deutsche Telekom. Daimler ended up 2.70 marks at 129.15.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6935 marks and 123.25 yen, compared with Thursday's late European levels of 1.7030 marks and 122.92 yen.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 26.6 points, or 0.6 percent, at 4,424.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 13.52 points, or 0.51 percent, at 2,645.62.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trade up 9.48 points, at 3,359.29. In later screen trade, the IBIS DAX ended up 36.47 points at 3,404.29.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed down 30 cents at $352.75. Silver finished three cents higher at $5.31.
